title: How a Corporate Travel Programmes Approval Standing Bears on a Cabin Move Co-Payment
content:
Where a Corporate Travel Programmes programme stands behind an Air Ticket Fare Brands booking, its approval arrangements and its billing standing together decide what share of the figure is carried forward on a cabin move.

## 1. The approval share

1.1 Where the programme carries 2 or more approval levels and its billing balance stands below its credit limit, the whole of the figure is carried forward: a share of 1.

1.2 Where the programme carries 1 approval level and no more, and its billing balance stands below its credit limit, the single-approval share of it is carried forward: 0.95, being 95 percent.

1.3 In every other case no such treatment applies to the share.

## 2. What is read, and from where

The approval levels and the credit limit are terms of the Corporate Travel Programmes programme standing against the booking, read from that programme's own record, as is the billing balance standing on it. Both of the first two rows require the balance to stand below the limit; a balance at the limit is not below it.

## 3. Truth table

| Approval levels the programme carries | Billing balance against the credit limit | Share carried forward |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2 or more | below the limit | 1 |
| exactly 1 | below the limit | 0.95 |
| 2 or more | at or above the limit | no such treatment |
| exactly 1 | at or above the limit | no such treatment |
| none | any | no such treatment |

## 4. Hypothetical readings

A programme carrying 3 approval levels with a billing balance of 4000.00 USD against a credit limit of 25000.00 USD carries the whole of the figure forward.

The same programme with a billing balance of 25000.00 USD is not below the limit, and no such treatment applies.

A programme carrying 1 approval level with a balance well below its limit carries 95 percent of the figure forward.
